subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining fix target the scheduled heartbeat/cron producer that asks for invalid workspace paths, or should OpenClaw change the generic read tool to treat directory paths as list operations?
rationale: Current source proves only partial fixes and one remaining read-tool failure shape; choosing the wrong layer could either miss the producer leak or broaden the model-facing tool contract.

options.title: Reproduce and fix the producer
options.body: Use a current-build gateway run to identify the scheduled producer, then keep read-tool semantics stable and correct the bad path/read request at its source.

options.title: Broaden read-tool semantics
options.body: Teach the read tool to handle directory paths as listings, but require explicit owner approval and tests because this changes the tool contract for all callers.

options.title: Hold for stronger logs
options.body: Keep the issue open without code work until a reporter or maintainer can provide current-main RSS and scheduler logs that identify the failing producer.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and fix the producer
recommendation.body: Use a current-build gateway run to identify the scheduled producer, then keep read-tool semantics stable and correct the bad path/read request at its source.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision crosses agent read-tool, cron, and heartbeat boundaries where this history shows broad adjacent work.
